questions: Which part of the plant catches the light?
Where do the roots grow, and what do they drink in?
segments.say: Parts of a green plant. Watch the leaf appear first, then the stem holding it up, and the roots spreading below the soil as water drops sink down to the root tips. Keep your student notes open at the leaf, stem and roots definitions for this scene.

questions: Which three ingredients arrive at the leaf?
What two products does the leaf make?
segments.say: Photosynthesis: plants make their own food. Watch the sunlight reach the leaf, the water drops travel up from the roots, and the carbon dioxide flow in from the air, then look for the food and the oxygen leaving. Now try the recipe question on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: What is broken down inside the leaf to release energy?
Which two substances are made by respiration?
segments.say: Respiration: the reverse process. Watch the food and oxygen move into the leaf, the energy sparks rise as the food is broken down, and the carbon dioxide and water leave. Check this against the respiration definition in your student notes before we move on.

questions: What moves in and out of the leaf in this scene?
Does that gas movement stop at night? How do you know?
segments.say: A common mistake: plants do not breathe? Watch the mistaken line being crossed out, then follow the gases moving in and out of the leaf first in the day and then at night. Finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this breathing trap.
segments.watchFor: Only animals breathe; plants do not. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the exit ticket: a plant has no nose, so its breathing is easy to miss. Send them back to scene s4 and to the correct turn: Plants take in and give out gases too: they respire all the time, day and night, just like us.

subject: science
title: Photosynthesis: how green plants make food
